feed.title: Making of Iltonggi
feed.subtitle: How Iltonggi is being made — one short note a day.

entry.title: Sure, Likely or Unknown
entry.summary: Every art check gets one of three labels. Here is what each label lets us do, and which findings we leave for a person to decide.

entry.title: Six New Towns and a Harder Normal Game
entry.summary: Six neutral towns in Act 3 pushed Normal win rates down to 14 percent. We changed only their troops, and this is how we picked the numbers.

entry.title: One Bow in a Hunting Mural
entry.summary: Our Goguryeo archer carried a long bow. Hunting murals show a short, curved bow, so we redrew it and wrote down how we checked.

entry.title: Three Difficulties, Held in Place by Numbers
entry.summary: How we simulate thousands of battles to keep Easy, Normal and Hard in their own win-rate ranges, and why the bot makes Hard look harder.

entry.title: How Big Is Too Big for a Phone Game?
entry.summary: Why we put a size budget on Iltonggi's art, sound and fonts, and the guard that fails the build when we go over.

entry.title: Picking Up Where You Left Off on Another Device
entry.summary: How Iltonggi lets you continue a game across Apple devices, and the rules we chose for when two devices disagree.

entry.title: A Save File That Survives Being Broken
entry.summary: How Iltonggi protects your progress if a save file is cut off mid-write, and how we tested it without breaking a real phone.

entry.title: Checking Our Own Pictures Against the Past
entry.summary: We compared Iltonggi's kings, ships and fortress art with murals and excavated objects, and wrote down what did not match.

entry.title: A Name and a Record, Nicknames and the Scoreboard
entry.summary: How the nickname and the records screen in Iltonggi work, what the four scoreboards count, and what is still being prepared.

entry.title: Ask Before You Pass, the Landowners of Act 10
entry.summary: Act 10 of Iltonggi has regions you cannot attack, and the reasons we turned a conquest game into a game of asking first.

entry.title: Two Brothers and One Table, Choosing a Side in Act 9
entry.summary: How Act 9 of Iltonggi turns a family quarrel in the Andes into a choice about which brother you stand beside.

entry.title: City on the Lake, What We Chose Not to Draw
entry.summary: Act 8 of Iltonggi, a map set on a lake in the highlands, and the lines we drew around what we would leave out of the picture.

entry.title: Three Seas, and the Cliff We Found by Simulation
entry.summary: Acts 4 to 6 in Iltonggi, and what two hundred simulated games per difficulty taught us about balance.

entry.title: From Three Kingdoms to a Wider Map, Where Iltonggi Stands Now
entry.summary: A plain look at how the acts of Iltonggi have grown beyond the Korean peninsula, what the world map does, and what is still being worked on.

entry.title: Your First 20 Turns, Five Things to Watch Early in a Land Grab
entry.summary: How to use troops, actions, scouting and diplomacy in your first Iltonggi game, with a focus on the early flow.

entry.title: From War Drums to Gayageum, We Made the Sounds Ourselves
entry.summary: How Iltonggi's 15 effects and 4 music tracks were synthesized by script with no outside audio, and why we remade some of them.

entry.title: Daegaya, 562: The Year the Last Gaya Closed
entry.summary: Eight years after Daegaya stood with Baekje at Gwansanseong, this is how the records say it fell to Silla in 562, and what kind of kingdom Gaya is in Iltonggi.

entry.title: The Day After You Take a Town: Designing the Aftermath of Conquest
entry.summary: What happens to population and mood right after you take a town in Iltonggi, and why we made sure that winning the battle is not the end of it.

entry.title: Hanji, Ink and the Seal: Choosing a Face for the Map
entry.summary: The materials and rules behind three look drafts for Iltonggi's map, redrawing the same land as clay wall, hanji paper and an old surveyor's sheet.

entry.title: Gwansanseong, 554: Where an Alliance Ended
entry.summary: Three years after the 551 Han River scenario, the Baekje-Silla alliance broke at Gwansanseong. Here is that scene, and where Iltonggi's diplomacy rules touch it.
